notes: The parts are the same as in step 1. I added no parts and dropped none.
The wiring diagram image was not provided. The connections follow the tutorial text: the driver is powered from 3.3V, and PWM on D4 sets the motor speed. GND is shared.

The catalogue card for the Grove I2C Mini Motor Driver has no PWM input pin. I connected D4 to the card's SCL pin, which stands in for the Grove signal line (yellow in the photo). This is an assumption.
The photo shows a Grove cable and a green adapter between the Nano and the driver. I modelled this as three jumper wires, as in step 1.
The Nano Matter and the driver module sit on the breadboard in the photo. I recorded them as resting on it without port-level breadboard connections, because their pin-to-hole placement isn't shown.
The DC motor's two leads go to the driver's OUT1 and OUT2. The motor's polarity does not matter.
The USB-C cable powers and programs the Nano Matter.
The catalogue lists the DC motor supply as 1.0-3.0 V. The driver's 3.3V rail powers it, as the tutorial specifies.
